title: Things to Do in Mahabaleshwar: Viewpoints, Strawberries, Temples & Forts
seoTitle: Things to Do in Mahabaleshwar: Views & Strawberries | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Mahabaleshwar: Arthur's Seat and Kate's Point, boating on Venna Lake, the Panchganga temple in Old Mahabaleshwar, strawberry farms, Pratapgad Fort, Lingmala Falls, Panchgani's Table Land, Tapola and the Kaas plateau in bloom.
dek: The highest hill station in the northern Western Ghats, with cliffside viewpoints, the source of five rivers, strawberry farms and a famous Maratha fort nearby.
searchIntent: Families and couples from Mumbai and Pune planning two or three days in Mahabaleshwar and Panchgani.

hero.caption: Arthur's Seat

intro: Mahabaleshwar, at about 1,350 metres in Satara district, was the summer capital of the Bombay Presidency under British rule. It sits on a plateau of the Sahyadris with deep valleys on every side, and Old Mahabaleshwar is sacred as the source of five rivers, including the Krishna.

The things to do in Mahabaleshwar include its famous viewpoints, boating on Venna Lake, temples in Old Mahabaleshwar, strawberry farms, and trips to Pratapgad Fort, Lingmala Falls, Panchgani and, in season, the flower meadows of the Kaas plateau.
Two to three days is ideal. October to June is the main season; strawberries are best from about December to March, and the heavy monsoon closes many points.

items.name: See Arthur's Seat
body: Arthur's Seat, named after a British officer, looks down into the deep Savitri valley on one side and the Jor valley on the other. It is often called the queen of Mahabaleshwar's points. Echo Point and Tiger Spring are on the way.

A short walk from the car park leads to the edge, and the paths continue to Window Point and Hunter Point. Mornings are clearest; clouds often fill the valleys after midday, which is beautiful in its own way.

items.name: Visit Kate's Point and Needle Hole
body: Kate's Point overlooks the Krishna valley and the Dhom and Balkawadi dams. Next to it, Needle Hole (Elephant's Head) point is a rock formation with a hole through it.

items.name: Watch sunrise at Wilson Point
body: Wilson Point (Sunrise Point), the highest point in Mahabaleshwar, has three platforms facing east for sunrise. Bombay Point, on the west, is the classic sunset viewpoint.

items.name: Go boating on Venna Lake
body: Venna Lake, built in 1842, has rowing and pedal boats, and pony rides and food stalls around it. Try corn on the cob and strawberries with cream from the stalls.

items.name: Visit Old Mahabaleshwar's temples
body: In Old Mahabaleshwar, the Panchganga Temple marks the source of five rivers, the Krishna, Koyna, Venna, Savitri and Gayatri, which flow from a stone cow's mouth into a tank. The Mahabaleshwar Temple, dedicated to Shiva, and the Krishnabai Temple, with its view over the Krishna valley, are nearby.

items.name: Pick strawberries
body: The Mahabaleshwar–Panchgani area grows most of India's strawberries. Farms around Gureghar and Bhilar welcome visitors to pick and buy in season, and shops sell jams, crushes and fudge. Bhilar is known as a village of books, with reading spaces in homes.

items.name: Shop at the main market
body: The main market sells strawberries, chikki, fudge, jams, leather chappals and walking sticks.

items.name: Explore Pratapgad Fort
body: Pratapgad, about 24 km away, was built by Shivaji in 1656 and is where he killed the Adil Shahi general Afzal Khan in 1659. It has ramparts, a Bhavani temple and a statue of Shivaji, with views over the Konkan.

The fort has upper and lower sections, with a statue of Shivaji on horseback, the Bhavani temple consecrated by him, and the tomb of Afzal Khan below the fort. The road there winds through forested ghats.

items.name: See Lingmala Falls
body: Lingmala Falls drops from a height of over 150 metres, best seen after the monsoon. A short walk leads to viewpoints.

items.name: Walk on Panchgani's Table Land
body: Panchgani, about 20 km away, has Table Land, a large flat laterite plateau with caves and views, as well as old boarding schools and Sydney Point.

items.name: See the Kaas plateau and Tapola
body: The Kaas plateau near Satara, part of the Western Ghats UNESCO site, is carpeted with wildflowers from about late August to October. Entry is limited and needs advance booking. Tapola, on the Shivsagar reservoir, offers boating and is sometimes called mini Kashmir.

facts.Best time: Late August to October for Kaas

items.name: October to February
body: Cool and clear, with strawberries from December and the best views from the points.

items.name: March to June
body: Warm days and cool nights; the peak season for families and the end of strawberry season.

items.name: July to September
body: Extremely heavy rain and fog; many points and shops close, though the waterfalls are spectacular.

byTraveller.text: Venna Lake, strawberry picking, Mapro-style food parks and the easy viewpoints.
Sunrise at Wilson Point, sunset at Bombay Point and a quiet stay in the forest.
Pratapgad Fort and the temples of Old Mahabaleshwar.
Leave early on Saturday, see the points and Venna Lake, and spend Sunday at Pratapgad or Panchgani before heading back.

oneDay: Watch sunrise at Wilson Point, then visit Arthur's Seat and Kate's Point. See Old Mahabaleshwar's temples before lunch, visit a strawberry farm in the afternoon and end with boating on Venna Lake.
tips: Mahabaleshwar is about four to five hours from Mumbai and three hours from Pune; Wathar is the nearest railway station.
The monsoon (June to September) is extremely wet, and many points and shops close.
Weekends and holidays bring heavy traffic; go on weekdays if you can.
Book Kaas plateau visits online in season.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Mahabaleshwar?
faqs.a: See Arthur's Seat, Kate's Point and Wilson Point, go boating on Venna Lake, visit Old Mahabaleshwar's temples, pick strawberries, explore Pratapgad Fort and visit Panchgani.

faqs.q: When is strawberry season in Mahabaleshwar?
How many days are enough for Mahabaleshwar?
Is Mahabaleshwar good in the monsoon?
faqs.a: It is very wet, foggy and many attractions close, though the greenery is dramatic. October to May is better for sightseeing.

faqs.q: How far is Pratapgad from Mahabaleshwar?
faqs.a: About 24 km, roughly 45 minutes by road.
